theory.intro: Every sine or cosine wave can be written as $y = k\sin\left(a(x-b)\right)+c$. The four constants set the **amplitude** $|k|$, the **period** $\dfrac{2\pi}{a}$, the **phase** (a horizontal translation of $b$) and the **mean position** $y=c$.
facts: The **mean position** is the line $y=c$, halfway between the maximum and the minimum.
The period of $y=k\sin(ax)$ and $y=k\cos(ax)$ is $\dfrac{2\pi}{a}$, and the period of $y=k\tan(ax)$ is $\dfrac{\pi}{a}$.
Read the phase only after $a$ has been factorised out, so $y=\sin\left(2x-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)$ is $y=\sin\left(2\left(x-\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)\right)$, a shift of $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$ right.
The range of $y=k\sin\left(a(x-b)\right)+c$ is $[\,c-|k|,\ c+|k|\,]$, because $\sin$ runs from $-1$ to $1$.
A negative $k$ reflects the curve in the $x$-axis, but the amplitude is still $|k|$.
$y=\tan x$ has no amplitude and no mean position, because it has no maximum and no minimum.
steps: Write the function in the form $y = k\sin\left(a(x-b)\right)+c$
State the amplitude, period, phase and mean position
Apply the dilations, then the translations
Sketch the mean position, then one cycle, then repeat it across the domain

\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}

State the amplitude, the period and the range of this function.
foundation.solution_text:

mastery.question_text:
The function $f(x) = 2\sin(2x)$ is defined only on $\dfrac{\pi}{8} \le x \le \dfrac{\pi}{3}$, as shown.
[tikz]
\begin{tikzpicture}[every node/.style={font=\large}]
\begin{axis}[axis lines=middle, xlabel={$x$}, ylabel={$y$},
  xmin=-0.08, xmax=1.3, ymin=-0.4, ymax=2.6,
  xtick={0.3927, 0.7854, 1.0472},
  xticklabels={$\frac{\pi}{8}$, $\frac{\pi}{4}$, $\frac{\pi}{3}$},
  ytick={1, 2},
  samples=200, clip=false,
  axis line style={-{Stealth}}, width=10cm, height=6.5cm]
\addplot[smooth, thick, blue, domain=0.3927:1.0472] {2*sin(deg(2*x))};
\addplot[only marks, mark=*, blue] coordinates {(0.3927,1.41421) (1.0472,1.73205)};
\end{axis}
\end{tikzpicture}
[/tikz]
Determine the range of $f(x)$ on this domain, giving exact values.
mastery.solution_text:
The greatest possible value occurs when $\sin(2x)=1$.
$2x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$
$x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$
This lies inside the domain, so the maximum value is $2$.
The minimum must then be at one of the endpoints.
$f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{8}\right) = 2\sin\dfrac{\pi}{4}$
$= \sqrt{2}$
$f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = 2\sin\dfrac{2\pi}{3}$
$= \sqrt{3}$
Since $\sqrt{2} < \sqrt{3}$, the smallest value is $\sqrt{2}$.
Range $=\left[\sqrt{2},\ 2\right]$
